title: The formation of black holes and singularities in spherically symmetric gravitational collapse
kind: primary paper (user-supplied PDF and extracted text)
version: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 44 (1991), 339–373; DOI 10.1002/cpa.3160440305
relevance: Specified spherical Einstein–massless-minimally-coupled-scalar model; Proposition 4.1 pp356–358 gives flat filled-cone region; Theorem 5.1 pp363–364 gives cone-data collapse criterion.
locator: printed p356, paragraph beginning 'In the following the spacetime is the future of the initial future null geodesic cone'; Proposition 4.1 pp356–358; Theorem 5.1 pp363–364
assumptions: Characteristic scalar data on central outgoing cone, radial constraints, and paper's stated asymptotic conditions. The analyzed spacetime is restricted to the future of the initial cone.
conclusion: Supports a flat region and collapse in the cone-generated future under the paper's hypotheses. Does not provide complete Cauchy data or assert exact flatness on the marked event's entire past in a maximal globally hyperbolic development.
proof_status: Source text checked at stated locators; coordinator supplied an existing deeper audit. This worker did not re-audit all proofs or cited well-posedness dependencies.
dependencies: Prior characteristic existence/uniqueness and global results cited by the paper; not independently audited here.
limits: The future-of-cone restriction is decisive for the full-past question. A local region or finite diamond cannot establish the maximal-development past quantifier.
open_questions: Can these particular cone data be embedded in complete smooth constraint-satisfying Cauchy data while preserving the cone solution and proving the full past footprint of b remains flat?

title: The problem of a self-gravitating scalar field
kind: primary paper (abstract checked through bibliographic record)
relevance: Early primary characteristic initial-value theory for the spherical massless Einstein–scalar system; identifies the starting hypersurface as a future light cone with central vertex.
locator: published-paper abstract; full proof and theorem locators not checked in this audit
assumptions: Spherically symmetric massless scalar; initial data on a future light cone with vertex at the centre, according to the abstract.
conclusion: Abstract reports local existence in retarded time and global uniqueness of classical solutions, with global classical dispersive evolution for sufficiently small data.
proof_status: Abstract-level only; theorem hypotheses and proof not verified.
limits: Abstract does not state a backward/exterior completion to a complete Cauchy development, nor preservation of the entire I^-(b). Do not interpret 'global uniqueness' as global-in-time existence or whole-past completion.
open_questions: Whether a precise theorem in the full paper provides a relevant compatible extension was not resolved; the checked abstract alone cannot support it.

title: Nonlinear stability of extremal Reissner–Nordström black holes in spherical symmetry
version: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 14 (2026), e3; DOI 10.1017/fmp.2025.10017; online 2025
relevance: Contains a precise local characteristic existence theorem useful for scoping what a local extension result says.
locator: §2.3.1, Proposition 2.5, printed pp21–22 (PDF pp21–22): smooth characteristic data with bounded C1 norms extend uniquely to a thin slab.
assumptions: Smooth bifurcate characteristic initial data for spherically symmetric Einstein–Maxwell–scalar system, with positive radius and conformal factor, constraints on both null initial segments, and bounded stated C1 norms.
conclusion: Existence and uniqueness of a smooth solution on a thin slab extending the characteristic data; higher norms bounded by appropriate higher-order data norms.
proof_status: Full text and proposition statement checked; proof is a short citation/iteration argument referencing prior local theory, not independently re-proved.
dependencies: The paper cites local characteristic existence and its generalized extension principle; dependency proofs not audited here.
limits: Different coupled matter system (Einstein–Maxwell–scalar, including charge); local finite slab only; no complete Cauchy extension, no asymptotically flat global matching, and no entire-past flatness theorem for the neutral Christodoulou cone solution.
open_questions: A neutral Einstein–massless-scalar result plus global data matching and complete causal-footprint control is still required.

title: Solutions to the Einstein-scalar-field system in spherical symmetry with large bounded variation norms
relevance: Theorem 1.7 constructs two-sided causally geodesically complete spherical Einstein–massless-scalar solutions from small smooth radiation data prescribed at past null infinity; compactly supported profiles yield a candidate exact-flat-past matched pair independently of collapse.
locator: §1.2, Theorem 1.7, printed pp5–6; characteristic setup and local uniqueness §2.1, printed pp7–8; construction uses u0→−∞ as described §1.2 and proved in §4; completeness §6.
assumptions: Smooth Φ:R→R; for some γ>0 and sufficiently small ε, integral bound ∫_u^v |Φ(v′)|dv′≤ε(v−u)^(1−γ) for all −∞<u≤v<∞, pointwise |Φ|+|Φ′|≤ε, and sup_v|Φ″|<∞. For nonzero compact support, choose 0<γ<1 and scale amplitude. The theorem constructs a solution on Q={(u,v):u∈R,u≤v<∞}, with regular center u=v and limiting data lim_{u→−∞}2∂_v(rφ)=Φ(v), lim_{u→−∞}∂_v r=1/2.
conclusion: For each γ>0 a sufficiently small ε gives a solution causally geodesically complete both to past and future. If Φ vanishes below v0, the approximating cone data are exactly Minkowski there; local uniqueness and the u0→−∞ limit imply the wedge v<v0 is exactly flat. Thus b=(t_b,t_b), t_b<v0, has entire chronological past in the flat wedge, matching the Φ=0 Minkowski comparison.
proof_status: Full-text selective audit of theorem, setup/local uniqueness, construction outline and completeness conclusion; flat-wedge claim is a derived corollary, not stated verbatim. No line-by-line reproof of §§3–6.
dependencies: Theorem 1.7 uses Theorem 1.1 estimates uniform in u0, a limiting construction in §4, and causal-geodesic-completeness arguments in §6.
limits: The theorem states two-sided causal geodesic completeness but does not expressly identify its solution as the MGHD of complete spacelike Cauchy data in Theorem 1.7. It does not match the specific Christodoulou 1991 cone data or establish a specified different observable along the central observer at fixed proper time.
open_questions: Verify global hyperbolicity/Cauchy-surface and MGHD identification in the contract's regularity category; select and prove a distinct future relational observable; separately assess finite-parameter control with specified incoming energy held fixed.

title: Volume Comparison for Hypersurfaces in Lorentzian Manifolds and Singularity Theorems
version: arXiv:1201.4249v1 (2012); published Annals of Global Analysis and Geometry 43 (2013), 233–251
relevance: Supplies the normal timelike maximizing-geodesic theorem used to test the proposed direct maximality argument for the complete scattering development.
locator: §2.2, Remark 2.4 and Theorem 2.5, preprint pp. 3–4: a Cauchy hypersurface in a globally hyperbolic spacetime is causally complete, and points in its future are joined to it by a proper-time maximizing timelike geodesic normal to the hypersurface; use the time-reversed statement for the past.
assumptions: Smooth globally hyperbolic Lorentzian spacetime and smooth spacelike acausal causally complete hypersurface; a Cauchy hypersurface is causally complete by Remark 2.4. The theorem's smooth category is sufficient for the quoted result.
conclusion: For each point in the causal future of the hypersurface there is a maximizing timelike geodesic from some point of the hypersurface, normal to it; the analogous past result follows by time reversal.
proof_status: Full-text selective check of the cited theorem, remark, and their use; no independent proof of Lorentzian causality results.
dependencies: The proof uses global hyperbolicity, compactness of the relevant causal set on the hypersurface, continuity of Lorentzian time separation, and standard maximizing-geodesic regularity.
limits: This result supplies only the normal-maximizer step. Applying it to Luk–Oh–Yang requires a common metric regularity category, a shared Cauchy-development embedding, and geodesic initial-value uniqueness; it does not itself identify that solution as an MGHD.
open_questions: Verify from a primary Einstein–scalar Cauchy uniqueness theorem that the source solution and any proposed larger development embed isometrically in a regularity class supporting this normal-maximizer theorem and ODE uniqueness.
